My research focuses on compound extreme events that threaten vulnerable populations in coastal and tropical regions worldwide. While individual extreme events pose severe risks, co-occurring hazards interact non-linearly to produce disproportionately high impacts, which are increasingly amplified by climate change. I study compound hazards driven by interactions across the atmosphere, ocean, and land—from synoptic-scale systems originating over the ocean that cause severe winds and flooding, to air–sea interactions driving extreme ocean warming and compounding coastal sea-level extremes. Ultimately, my goal is to turn these scientific insights into actionable tools, such as an automated system I developed that is now used operationally by a national meteorological agency for real-time hazard forecasting and risk mitigation.
